title: Handoff Journeyboard Weekly Inspection
content:
Purpose: informal weekly inspection of oncall handoffs, two small incidents, and SLO drift that surfaced during night shifts. This is a working note — gaps, TODOs, and hypothesis sections intentionally left half-formed for the next shift to pick up.

TL;DR:
- Two short incidents this week; both mitigated quickly. No customer-visible downtime, but recurring tail latency spikes for model shards.
- SLO snapshot: 99.7% p99 within target (target 99.9%) for the 7-day window; drift correlates with KV cache eviction storms during long-sequence workloads.
- Immediate handoff checklist updated with new KV cache knob to try during noisy auto-scale events.

Summary of events (timeline):
- 2029-04-16 03:22 UTC — Incident RW-INC-2029-1145: p99 latency spike in hosted inference route /v1/chat for region: eu-west-1. Triggered pager, bridge opened. Initial symptom: steady stream of slow requests (p95->p99), worker metrics show abrupt KV cache miss rate jump and increased memory churn on infer-g1 pods.
  - Mitigation steps taken: scaled infer-g1 pool + applied temporary throttle on long-sequence requests (seq > 1200) via routing rule. Brought p99 back under threshold in ~9 minutes.
  - Root-cause hypothesis (interim): a)) background housekeeping job on storage node S3-sync triggered large object re-reads causing network congestion to GPU hosts OR b)) a quantized model variant fallback caused larger-than-usual KV entries and increased cache pressure. Need trace logs to confirm.
  - Notes: applied manual eviction policy (ttl 20s) to secondary kv namespace to relieve memory pressure; removal flagged as a temporary emergency config.

- 2029-04-16 18:05 UTC — Ops noise: autoscaler misfired during a short but intense synthetic traffic spike from customer test harness RW-OPS-3456. Resulted in 2x cold starts and a transient spike in tail latency for dedupe route. No page. Followed by a billing spike alert (billing-warn) that flagged heavy retry traffic.
  - Action: reached out to Solutions Eng to contain rogue test, added rate limit exception and noted to add a guard in the autoscaler to ignore synthetic-signed test tokens.

SLO / metrics snapshot (7d rolling):
- p50: 26ms (target 30ms)
- p95: 138ms (target 150ms)
- p99: 910ms (target 700ms) -> current shortfall driven by cache-eviction episodes and cold-starts
- error rate: 0.03% (well below 0.2% threshold)
- availability: 99.996%

Observed signals and correlations:
- KV cache miss-rate correlates strongly with p99 latency spikes when sequence length distribution shifts right (customers sending longer contexts). See attached metrics (linked below).
- Memory churn and kernel context-switches on infer-g1 hosts appear to co-occur with network egress bursts to object storage (varnish-like behaviour).
- Autoscaler thresholding currently uses 60s lookback; short synthetic bursts create flapping.

Immediate mitigations and config changes applied (ephemeral):
- Temporary route-level throttle for sequences >1200 for eu-west-1 (rollback planned after 48h observation). Ticket: RW-OPS-3489.
- Reduced secondary KV namespace TTL to 20s to limit memory accumulation during high churn windows. (Reverted if regressions).
- Manual bump of infer-g1 pool by +25% for 3 hours during peak maintenance window.

Handoff checklist updates (what next on Monday AM shift):
- Verify rollback hooks: ensure TTL change is recorded in config audit and Revert playbook (runbook ref RW-runbook-kv-evictions).
- Start trace-sampling at 100% for /v1/chat in eu-west-1 for 1 hour to capture full KV cache lifecycle for impacted requests.
- Verify whether the storage housekeeping job overlapped the incident window (check infra-scheduler logs, job id possibly: infra-hs-20290416-02).
- Add autoscaler guard to ignore tokens matching test harness signature (Pattern: RW-TEST-*). Put as a quick patch: autoscale-ignore-list.
- Add a simple sequencelength-aware routing rule to separate long-context requests to a lower-cost variant with pre-warmed instances. (Design spike required).

Longer-term follow-ups and owners: (estimate / backlog prioritization)
- Investigate root cause of KV cache pressure (owner: Luca) — collect trace-level artifacts and map object sizes in kv store. Target: next week deep-dive.
- Autoscaler resilience improvements (owner: Samira) — add debounce window and synthetic-token exclusion. Feasibility spike: 3 days.
- Pre-warm strategy for long-sequence inference (owner: Omar) — experiment with mini-pools pinned to quantized variants. Prototype by EoQ.
- Add regression alert tied to per-route KV miss-rate that fires before p99 breach (owner: Maya)

Notes to next oncall (direct):
- If you see repeated p99 spikes after a TTL rollback, re-enable full-sampled tracing and escalate to infra-networking (channel #infra-egress).
- Avoid broad TTL changes during EU peak hours; prefer targeted namespace adjustments.
- If autoscaler triggers >3 times in 10 minutes, open a P1 and start bridge immediately — flapping autoscale correlates with client retry storms.

Open questions / hypothesis bank (for investigation):
- Did a model fall-back to a different quantized kernel increase KV footprint per request? Confirm with model-catalog logs and variant rollouts around 2029-04-16 03:00–04:00 UTC.
- Is object-store re-read latency causing kernel stall on GPU host? Likely if network queues fill. Need netstat/ifconfig dumps correlated with kernel logs.
- Could a GC/compaction in the secondary kv backend be scheduled during EU night windows? Check maintenance windows.

Meeting notes / sync items for Friday triage (2029-04-19):
- Deep-dive scheduled 2029-04-19 16:00 UTC (30m) — agenda: attach traces, compare kv sizes, review autoscaler logs, decisions on pre-warm prototype. Invites to include: eng-sre, serving-runtime, infra-networking, solutions-eng.
- Deliverable: prioritized action list and an A/B test plan for sequencelength-aware routing.

Appendix (quick links):
- Incident ticket RW-INC-2029-1145 (pager notes and timeline)
- Autoscaler history RW-OPS-3456
- KV runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/kv-cache-runbook
- Slack: #sre-eu oncall, #infra-egress

Quick raw logs excerpts (copied here for convenience):
- "2029-04-16T03:21:57Z infer-g1-7f4b: kv-miss-rate increased from 4.2% -> 37.9% within 90s"
- "2029-04-16T03:23:12Z network-egress host-120: retransmits spike 12x baseline"

Scratch / notes-to-self:
- Try a controlled run with synthetic long sequences but with cold cache to reproduce. Use small subset of EU infra to avoid broader noise.
- Add a monitoring dashboard tile for per-namespace cache size and eviction rate.

Action items (short):
- [Luca] Collect full trace dump + model variant logs (due 2029-04-18).
- [Samira] Autoscaler debounce patch PR and quick test (due 2029-04-22).
- [Omar] Design doc stub for pre-warm pool and sequencelength routing (due 2029-04-30).
- [Maya] Create regression alert for KV-miss -> p99 coupling (due 2029-04-19).

End of notes.

-- Maya (oncall)
